knowledge_graph.title: Factitious disorder
knowledge_graph.description: A factitious disorder is a mental disorder in which a person, without a malingering motive, acts as if they have an illness by deliberately producing, feigning, or exaggerating symptoms, purely to attain a patient's role.

related_questions.question: How do you treat factitious disorder?

text_blocks.snippet: Factitious disorder is challenging to treat because individuals often deny their symptoms or the underlying psychological issues. Treatment typically involves psychotherapy, such as cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), to address thinking patterns and behaviors, and family therapy to educate loved ones and improve family dynamics. While medications aren't used to treat the disorder itself, they may be prescribed for co-occurring conditions like depression or anxiety. The primary goal of treatment is to reduce harm, manage symptoms, and address the root causes of the behavior.
snippet_highlighted_words: psychotherapy, such as cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), to address thinking patterns and behaviors, and family therapy to educate loved ones and improve family dynamics

list.title: Psychotherapy:
list.snippet: CBT and other forms of psychotherapy help individuals identify and change negative thought patterns and behaviors contributing to the disorder.

list.title: Family Therapy:
list.snippet: This can help family members understand the condition and learn how to support the individual without reinforcing unhealthy behaviors, according to the Cleveland Clinic.

list.title: Medication:
list.snippet: Medications are not used to treat factitious disorder itself, but they can be prescribed to manage co-occurring conditions like depression, anxiety, or other mental health issues.

list.title: Addressing Underlying Causes:
list.snippet: Treatment also focuses on identifying and addressing the underlying psychological issues, such as past trauma or relationship problems, that may be contributing to the disorder.

list.title: Harm Reduction:
list.snippet: A crucial aspect of treatment is reducing the misuse or overuse of medical resources and preventing self-harm or other harmful behaviors.

list.title: Denial:
list.snippet: Many individuals with factitious disorder deny they have a problem, making it difficult to engage them in treatment.

list.title: Lack of Motivation:
list.snippet: Some individuals may not be motivated to change their behavior or seek help.

list.title: Revolving Door:
list.snippet: Patients may seek treatment from multiple healthcare providers, leading to a cycle of testing and treatment without addressing the core issue.

list.title: Interprofessional Approach:
list.snippet: Effective treatment often involves a team of healthcare professionals, including psychiatrists, psychologists, primary care physicians, and social workers, according to the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

list.title: Non-Confrontational Approach:
list.snippet: Confronting patients directly can lead to defensiveness and termination of treatment. Instead, a compassionate and non-judgmental approach is recommended, according to the UM Health-Sparrow.

list.title: Safety:
list.snippet: In cases where the individual is at risk of self-harm or harm to others, treatment may involve psychiatric hospitalization.

list.title: Family Involvement:
list.snippet: Family therapy and support are crucial for helping the individual and their loved ones cope with the disorder and develop healthier behaviors, according to the Cleveland Clinic.
